I do not see one completely replacing the other. Instead, the market is choosing between Ethereum's decentralized application dominance and Ripple's targeted institutional infrastructure. Your choice depends entirely on which network architectural model wins the multi year regulatory and adoption race.

translatedData.content:
Here are some hard truths for new friends; listen up to save yourself a few grand.

When you first enter the crypto scene, stop dreaming about doubling your money. If you don’t even set a stop-loss, why do you think you can make a profit?

First, don’t use your living expenses to trade. If you’re betting money you can’t afford to lose, your mindset is bound to crash. If you lose, you’ll hesitate to cut your losses; if you win, you won’t be able to hold onto your gains. Use spare cash so you can stay cool-headed. $BTC 

Second, don’t jump straight into contracts. With 100x leverage, just a small spike can wipe you out. Even if you didn’t get the direction wrong, your money could vanish. Start with spot trading, learn to read trends, set stop-losses, and then think about leverage.

Third, don’t trust signal groups. The screenshots they flaunt might be fabricated, or just the one profitable trade out of ten. If you dive in, you’re just picking up the bags.

Fourth, don’t go all in. Split your capital into ten parts, and only test the waters with one part at a time. If you lose one part, you still have nine left. If you go all in and it hits zero, there won’t be a next time.

Fifth, if you make a profit, withdraw half right away. The numbers in your account are just digits; only what you withdraw is yours. Stop thinking about compound interest; once you have cash in hand, your mindset stabilizes.

The crypto space isn’t lacking opportunities; what it lacks is you still being alive. First, learn not to lose, then talk about making money. These few words could save you from liquidation, believe it or not.

In the futures market, 
what truly holds value isn't guts, but control $IRYS 

I've seen the bravest traders, opening positions with $5000 at 50x leverage, only to get liquidated in a day. I've also seen 'chicken' traders, who only take 5% of their capital with 5x leverage, and they've never been liquidated in three years. Those with big guts have long exited the market, while the cautious ones are still steadily raking in profits.

In the futures market, guts aren't worth much. Being willing to gamble, to hold, or to go all in isn't the real skill. The true value lies in control—controlling your hands to avoid reckless trades, controlling your mind to refrain from adding to profits, and controlling your emotions to prevent revenge trading.

I have a follower who went long on ETH last year with a floating profit of $8000. He was so excited that he wanted to increase his position. I told him to hold back: first, withdraw his initial capital, and let the profits keep rolling in. He followed my advice. Later, when ETH pulled back, he lost half his profit, but he had already gotten his initial capital back, keeping his mindset stable. He said, "If I hadn't controlled myself and added to my position, I might have lost everything during that pullback."

#ETH  In the crypto game, it's not really about the cash. Even if I hit 48 million, I still feel like it's not enough to spend. 
It's not about showing off; many who have been through it understand this feeling. 
Let me give you a quick background: 
Born in the 90s, graduated from university and moved to Shenzhen, entered the crypto space in 2014. 
Now I'm in Guangzhou, with two houses and two cars, 
spending 100k a month feels like nothing, 
most of my assets are still parked on exchanges. 
But let's be real—trading isn’t romantic anymore. 

Those who have been in the market for the long haul 
have long moved past the phase of "happy when it goes up, sleepless when it drops." 
What’s left are three words: 
repetition, monotony, and battling oneself. 
1. Staying up late isn’t a big deal for us 
For traders, the market is the alarm clock. 
Day and night are the same. 
You’ll notice many so-called “young pros,” 
they're not old, but they look like they’ve aged a decade. 
Your body and emotions are just traded for experience. 
I’d say I’m on the disciplined side. 

2. Stop dreaming about a life of excess 
The reality is more about “going through the motions.” 
Even when I go out to relax, 
there's always a string of tension in my mind. 
It’s not greed; it’s a sense of responsibility. 
The more people trust you, the less you can afford to stop. 
Most of the time isn’t socializing, 
but monitoring the charts, reading sentiment, reviewing, and reflecting. 
Messages on my phone? They never stop piling up. 

3. Pressure never disappears; it just escalates 
At first, I learned how to relieve stress, 
then I practiced how to bear it. 
Answering questions, explaining logic, calibrating positions, 
those who understand know— 
a single point can make a world of difference. 
Finally, here are a few principles I always stick to: 
1️⃣ Don’t rely on feelings; respect the current market sentiment. 
2️⃣ Always have stop-losses; structure and capacity are both essential. 
3️⃣ If the logic is right, take it; if wrong, admit it. 
4️⃣ Trading isn’t about who’s the toughest; it’s about who can go the distance. 
In the end, I found that trading is never about the skills, 
but about managing human nature. 
I hope whoever reads this can slowly outpace 
the one person who can hold you back the most: yourself.

content:
#ETH  币圈最难赢的根本不是钱、哪怕赚到 4800 万，我依然觉得钱不太够花。
不是凡尔赛，是很多经历过的人都会懂的那种感觉。
简单交代下背景：
90 年男，大学毕业去了深圳，2014年进圈。
现在在广州，两套房、两辆车，
每个月拿出 10 万消费基本无感，
大部分资产依然留在交易所。
但说句掏心窝子的——
交易这件事，早就不浪漫了。

真正长期泡在市场里的人，
早就过了“涨一点就开心、跌一点就失眠”的阶段。
剩下的只有三个词：
重复、枯燥、对抗自己。
一、所谓熬夜，在我们这不算什么
对交易员来说，行情就是闹钟。
白天黑夜没有区别。
你会发现很多所谓的“年轻高手”，
年纪不大，却看着比同龄人老一截。
身体和情绪，都是拿来换经验的。
我算比较自律的那一类。

二、别再幻想天天灯红酒绿
真实状态更多是“随便应付”。
就算出去放松，
脑子里也始终绷着一根线。
不是贪，是责任感。
信任你的人越多，你越不敢停。
多数时间不是应酬，
而是盯盘、看情绪、复盘、反思。
手机消息？永远清不完。

三、压力从来不会消失，只会升级
最开始学的是“怎么减压”，
后来练的是“怎么扛压”。
回复问题、解释逻辑、校准位置，
懂的人都知道——
差一个点位，结果天差地别。
最后，说几条我一直死守的原则：
1️⃣ 不靠感觉，尊重当下的市场情绪
2️⃣ 必须有止损，结构和承受力缺一不可
3️⃣ 逻辑对就拿，错了就认
4️⃣ 交易不是比谁猛，是比谁走得远
走到最后才发现，
交易拼的从来不是技术，
而是对人性的管理能力。
希望刷到这篇的你，都能在市场里，
慢慢赢过那个，
最容易拖你后腿的自己。

Small capital doesn't fail because it's little,
It fails because of these three things

A buddy of mine had just 800U and wanted to flip it. He jumped right in with a 20x contract, made 200U on the first day, and was over the moon. The next day, the market pulled back, and he didn't cut losses—he held on. By the third day, he got liquidated, left with under 100. He asked me, 'Is it because I had too little money?' I said, 'No, it's not the money; you made three fatal mistakes. $BTC 

First, dying from 'urgency.' Small accounts often want to double up in one shot, opening high leverage, going all in, chasing meme coins. The more urgent you are, the easier it is to lose. Being rushed clouds your judgment; when it's time to cut losses, you think, 'Just hold a bit longer,' and when you should be in cash, you think, 'Let me gamble again.' If you’re not in a hurry, that 800U can grow slowly; when you rush, it's just cannon fodder.

Second, dying from 'greed.' After making some profit, you can't bear to leave, always wanting 'just a bit more.' When profits drop from 200U to 100U, you're still waiting; at 50U, you're even more reluctant to cut. In the end, it all goes to zero. Think about it: doubling 800U only gets you to 1600U; is it worth risking it all?

Third, dying from 'holding on.' You don’t exit when you’re losing, comforting yourself with 'it will come back.' Holding on once might work, but holding on ten times will eventually lead to a liquidation. That little principal can't withstand one big hold. $ETH 

If small capital wants to survive, just three rules: don’t rush, don’t be greedy, don’t hold on. Stick to the rules, take small amounts each time to test the waters; losses won't hurt, and when you make a gain, just run. Survive, and the money will gradually roll in.

Newbies trading futures, first learn to survive, then think about making money#新手必看 

Don't jump in and immediately fixate on "doubling" your money. If you don't even understand how to avoid liquidation, why do you think you can profit?

I've seen the wildest newbies: entering with 1000U, going all in with 20x leverage, and not setting a stop-loss. Three days later, they're liquidated and come asking, "Is the market bad?" I tell them it's not the market; they didn't even leave themselves a safety net.

For newbies trading futures, there are three survival rules; if you can't remember them, don't even touch it.$ETH 

First, split your funds into small portions. Take 1000U and break it into 10 parts, only risking 100U per trade. If you lose that 100U, stop—no moving to the next chunk. If you go all in and get wiped out, there won’t be a next time.

Second, don’t leverage over 5x. Within 5x, you have some breathing room. Above 20x, even a small fluctuation can wipe you out.

Third, set your stop-loss in stone. The first thing after opening a position is to set a stop-loss at 1.5%; if it hits, cut it. No fantasies, don’t wait for a rebound.

Practice with 100U, aiming for three months without liquidation. Once you master that, then we can talk about making money. If you can’t manage that, giving you 10,000U would just be a waste.

Newbie lesson one: learn how not to die first. Surviving is the only way to flip your position.$BTC 

Follow Kun Ge, no boasting, no empty promises, just sharing real experiences that can help you stay in the market.#BTC #ETH #ZEC #BILL

#ETH  No one starts off as a master. My journey in crypto trading, from losing sleep over losses and questioning life after a crash, to now consistently cashing out over a million every month, isn't due to talent or luck, but solid skills and strategies honed through real trading experience. Today, I'm sharing these free, simple, executable, and effective strategies for those in the crypto space.

1. Capital Rules: To make money, first, protect your capital

No matter how good your strategy, it’s useless if you can’t withstand a liquidation. 
Portfolio thinking: With a 50k capital, only risk 5k on each trade, keeping total exposure under 20%. 
Set stop-losses: Cut losses at 2% without hesitation, no holding onto losing trades. Avoid high leverage: Newbies should steer clear of leverage, and even seasoned traders shouldn't exceed 10% exposure. Just this rule can help you dodge most liquidation events.

2. Core Strategy: Less is More
The market doesn’t reward you for ‘doing more’; it rewards you for ‘doing it right.’ 
One-way trades: Only go long or short, avoid flipping positions, which significantly boosts your win rate. 
Mechanical discipline: Pre-set your stop-loss at 3% and take-profit at 5%, which is more reliable than making on-the-spot judgments. 
Control your trading frequency: The first 1-2 trades each day are usually the highest quality; anything beyond 3 trades is essentially giving away money.

3. Warning Zones: 90% of newbies fall into these traps
Never add to a losing position: Each time you average down, you’re one step closer to liquidation. 
Minimize meaningless trades: Fees can eat up a large chunk of your profits. 
Taking profits is essential: Most liquidations stem from the belief that “it should go up more.” 
Case comparison: With the same 100k, the outcomes can be drastically different. 
Mistaken approach: 
Full position + high leverage → averaging down on a drop → holding onto losing trades leading to liquidation.
Correct approach: 
Use only 20k for your base position → 3% stop-loss / 5% take-profit → only execute two high-quality trades a week. 
Outcome: Monthly returns can stabilize at 8%, with compound annual growth exceeding 150%.

Expert Mantra: Remember these six rules
Do: Use spare cash, stick to discipline, trade one direction. 
Don’t: Go all in, hold losing positions, or block both sides. 
Final reminder: Contracts are not a casino. 
Those who gamble their living expenses for future gains often end up losing everything. 
Only by safeguarding your capital and surviving long enough will you earn the right to talk about big money in the crypto space.

title: 🚨 ¡PÁSALO RÁPIDO! El colapso financiero que nadie quiere que recuerdes ⚠️
subTitle:
Wall Street 1929 vs. El Mundo Cripto: ¿Dos caras de la misma moneda?
A simple vista, el colapso de Wall Street en 1929 y los brutales "cripto inviernos" parecen sacados del mismo libreto financiero. Sin embargo, aunque la psicología humana detrás de ambos mercados es idéntica (avaricia extrema seguida de pánico absoluto), las reglas del juego y las dinámicas son profundamente diferentes.
Las Similitudes: La anatomía de la euforia
La trampa del dinero prestado (Apalancamiento): En los años 20, los ciudadanos compraban acciones pagando solo el 10% en efectivo y pidiendo prestado el 90% restante. Cuando el mercado bajó, los corredores exigieron los pagos y la estructura colapsó. En el ecosistema cripto ocurre algo idéntico: el uso excesivo de apalancamiento (operar con dinero prestado por los *exchanges*) suele detonar cascadas de liquidaciones masivas que hunden los precios en cuestión de minutos.
 La fiebre de las masas: Tanto en 1929 como en las grandes burbujas cripto (como los picos de 2017 o 2021), el catalizador fue la narrativa del "enriquecimiento rápido". Personas sin conocimientos financieros entraron en masa al mercado impulsadas por el miedo a quedarse fuera (*FOMO*), inflando una burbuja insostenible.
Las Diferencias: Velocidad tradicional vs. Volatilidad cuántica
Característica Crac de Wall Street (1929) Colapsos del Mundo Cripto
Velocidad del ciclo Lenta. Tardó casi 3 años en tocar su fondo más bajo en 1932.  Ultra veloz. Los analistas señalan que las criptomonedas concentran ciclos históricos de auge y caída en pocos meses. 
Magnitud de caídas El Dow Jones cayó un 89% en su punto máximo de crisis. Bitcoin ha sufrido caídas del -92% (2011), -85% (2015) y -75% (2022), recuperándose siempre. 
Regulación Prácticamente nula antes del crac, lo que obligó a fundar la SEC después.  En constante evolución; transitando de un salvaje oeste a una creciente adopción institucional (como los ETF de Bitcoin). 
Respaldo Empresas con fábricas, empleados y producción real en la economía. | Activos digitales descentralizados basados en blockchain, cuyo valor depende netamente de la oferta, la demanda y la confianza en su utilidad. |
¿Podría volver a suceder un desplome similar?
Sí, un colapso de magnitudes similares o peores puede volver a ocurrir. De hecho, la pregunta no es *si* sucederá, sino *cuándo* y *dónde*.
En el mercado financiero tradicional:
Hoy en día existen disyuntores automáticos (mecanismos que congelan las operaciones si la bolsa cae drásticamente en un solo día) diseñados específicamente para evitar el pánico ciego de 1929. No obstante, el riesgo actual no está en las acciones individuales, sino en la interconexión del sistema global, el endeudamiento de los gobiernos y la velocidad del *trading* algorítmico, donde las inteligencias artificiales pueden vender miles de millones de dólares en milisegundos, provocando "Flash Crashes" (caídas relámpago).
En el mercado de las criptomonedas:
Las correcciones agresivas del 50% al 80% son, paradójicamente, parte de la naturaleza cíclica normal de este ecosistema. Sin embargo, a medida que grandes fondos de inversión e instituciones financieras tradicionales inyectan capital en las criptomonedas, el riesgo cambia. Ya no se trata de un mercado aislado: un colapso sistémico total en el mundo cripto podría tener hoy un efecto dominó que arrastre a la economía tradicional, algo que no ocurría hace una década.
La tecnología cambia, los activos evolucionan, pero el miedo y la codicia humana siguen intactos.
 💬 Debate abierto para la comunidad:
Considerando que el Bitcoin y las criptomonedas sufren caídas que harían temblar al Wall Street de 1929 pero siempre han logrado recuperarse y marcar nuevos máximos, ¿creen que la volatilidad extrema es el precio justo a pagar por un sistema financiero descentralizado, o llegará el día en que una regulación masiva apague definitivamente este mercado? ¡Los leo en los 
#bitcoin #criptos #ada #eth #panic 
comentarios! 👇

There's a weird phenomenon in the crypto scene: the harder it drops during the day, the safer it tends to be at night.

This isn't some mystical thing; it's a rule I've figured out from watching the charts for five years. $LAB 

During the day, we mainly have the Asian and European sessions, where retail traders are heavily influenced by emotions. Any little dip sends them rushing to cut losses, leading to panic selling. But after 9:30 PM, when the US markets open, institutional money comes in, liquidity improves, and prices often get supported. The harder it drops during the day, the more likely it is to bounce back at night.

Last year, there was a time when ETH dropped 8% during the day, and the group was in a frenzy. I placed a low buy order, setting my stop-loss just below the day’s low by 2%. When the US markets opened at night, ETH bounced back by 12% from its low, and I made a cool 15% profit and walked away.

But not all coins can be played this way. This strategy only works for major coins like BTC and ETH that have depth and institutional participation. Altcoins tend to drop during the day and keep dropping at night—stay away from those.

How to play it? When there's a big drop during the day (like over 5%), wait for the 15-minute candlestick chart to show signs of stabilization (long lower wicks, increased volume stopping the drop), and place a small order for a bounce with 5x leverage, setting your stop-loss just below the day’s lowest price. Aim to take profits when it bounces back to halfway of the drop. If it hasn’t bounced back by 10 PM, pull your order—it means the institutions aren’t showing up. $BTC 

Remember: this is about catching a bounce, not bottom fishing. Stick to your stop-loss; if you're wrong, just get out. A harsh drop during the day isn’t a bad thing; it’s an opportunity.

Those who have never been liquidated find it hard to truly respect the market. I was the same back in the day; when my account doubled, I felt like a genius. Full margin, high leverage, no stop-loss, thinking about doubling again before calling it a day. Then came a pullback, and I lost all my profits, plus some of my principal. #新手必看 

After that liquidation, I stared at the numbers for a long time. It wasn't about feeling sorry; I wanted to remember that feeling. Later, every time I thought about going in heavy, I recalled that feeling. I hesitated, took lighter positions. But the key wasn't just that. I realized there were actually several chances to escape before the liquidation. The first pullback, my loss wasn't significant; if I had exited, it would have been fine. I didn't exit. The second pullback, my loss increased; I could have exited then as well. Still didn't exit. By the third time, I couldn’t exit at all. It wasn't that the market didn't give me opportunities; it was me missing those chances time after time.

Later, I set a rule: if the market gives me three chances to exit and I don’t, it’s not the market’s fault; it's my execution that’s off. Since then, before entering any position, I first plan my escape route. At what price do I exit, and at what loss do I exit? Think it through before entering. Those who can't even think through their losses won’t have lasting wins.

That night of the liquidation, I sat on my balcony pondering for a long time. It wasn't about how to get back to break-even; it was about what I was actually doing. I realized that I wasn't trading; I was gambling. Gamblers only look at wins; traders first consider losses. From that day on, I changed. I didn’t become more skilled; I became more cautious. A bit more cautious, and I’ll last longer.

title: Can Feel Your Pain: The Altcoin Market Has Broken Trust
subTitle:
The Painful Reality of the Altcoin Market

The altcoin market has become an environment where retail investors are expected to absorb endless losses while whales, market makers, bots, and leveraged traders dominate the game.

Every cycle starts with excitement:
new narratives, influencer hype, promises of “financial freedom,” and dreams of life-changing gains.

But zoom out on the monthly charts of most altcoins and the reality becomes hard to ignore:
years of red candles, collapsing liquidity, dead communities, and investors trapped holding assets down 80%, 90%, even 99% from their highs.

Meanwhile, large holders and sophisticated traders often thrive in this chaos. Whales can move price with relatively little effort in low-liquidity markets. Sudden pumps attract retail buyers, only for aggressive sell pressure to crush momentum again. Futures traders and automated bots profit repeatedly by shorting rallies, liquidating emotional traders at every level.

Retail investors are constantly told to “be patient” and “keep holding,” but many are asking a valid question now:

Why would ordinary people continue participating in a market where long-term holding so often leads to destruction?

If the average participant experiences:

massive drawdowns,

constant manipulation,

insider advantages,

dilution from endless token unlocks,

and extreme volatility designed to liquidate leverage,

then what kind of healthy market structure is this supposed to be?

A market cannot survive long-term on hope alone while trust keeps eroding.

There is also a deeper concern:
Is this environment actually healthy for the future of crypto?

If retail investors repeatedly enter the market only to become exit liquidity for larger players, eventually many stop coming back. Confidence disappears. Communities fracture. Genuine innovation gets overshadowed by short-term extraction and speculative games.

Crypto was originally sold as an alternative financial system — one that would empower ordinary people. But for many participants in the altcoin market, the experience has felt more like surviving an endless cycle of hype, manipulation, and disappointment.

At some point, the industry has to ask itself:
If retail always loses, who is left to believe in the future.
#BTC #ETH

title: ETH Drops Under $2,200: What to Watch Now
subTitle:
Ethereum has reached the bottom of its descending 4-hour channel at the same time its daily MA50 has crossed above price, and the two conditions are not independent: one defines where ETH is, and the other defines what it must clear to go anywhere higher.

Key Takeaways
ETH at $2,193.MA50 flipped from support to resistance after price broke below it.Ali Charts: ETH at 4H channel bottom, watching for bounce to $2,280 or $2,390..MA50 at $2,254 sits between current price and first target of $2,280.MA100 at $2,149 sits $30 below the channel bottom at $2,180.
How the MA50 flipped
The ETH/USDT shows Ethereum dropping to $2,193 at the time of writing, down 3% for the day, while the MA structure tells the story of the past six weeks in precise terms.

During the April recovery that took ETH from approximately $1,950 to $2,500, the MA50 was rising below price and acting as support. Price held above the MA50 on multiple daily closes during that rally, and the MA50's rising trajectory confirmed the recovery's validity. That relationship has now inverted.
The MA50 at $2,254 spent the April recovery acting as rising support that price held above on multiple daily closes; it is now $61 above current price and acting as resistance, which means the same level that once defined the floor of the recovery has become the ceiling of the current decline. The inversion happened as price declined through May, eventually crossing below the MA50 and leaving it overhead. A moving average that has recently acted as support carries more weight as resistance than an arbitrary price level, because participants who established positions near that level during the recovery are now sitting at a loss and may reduce exposure on any return toward their entry price.
The MA100 at $2,149 sits $44 below current price and is the next structural support on the daily chart. The MA200 at $2,611 is $417 overhead and remains a distant declining resistance. RSI at 39.98 has crossed below 40, a level that on the daily timeframe has historically marked the boundary of short-term oversold conditions, against a signal of 51.12, a spread of 11.14 points, confirming daily momentum is net-negative.
What Ali Charts' channel analysis adds
Ali Charts published a 4-hour Ethereum chart annotated with a descending channel, showing price at $2,191 touching the channel's lower boundary. The channel has four labeled reference points: the bottom at approximately $2,180–$2,191 where price currently sits, a lower mid-range at $2,230, an upper mid-range at $2,280, and the channel top at $2,390. Ali Charts is watching for a spike in buying pressure at the channel bottom that could send price toward $2,280 or $2,390.
https://twitter.com/alicharts/status/2055554607988785510
Ali Charts' mid-range target of $2,280 sits $25 above the MA50 at $2,254, meaning the bounce he is watching for at the channel bottom must clear a resistance level before it reaches its first destination, and a bounce that stalls at the MA50 would produce a lower high within the descending channel rather than a recovery toward the top. The channel's descending structure means every bounce that fails to reach the top creates a lower high, which progressively compresses the range and increases the significance of the channel bottom as a support level.
What the MA100 and channel bottom say together
The MA100 at $2,149 sits $30 below Ali Charts' channel bottom at $2,180, creating a structural cushion where two independent support references converge within a narrow range: if the channel bottom holds, the MA100 never gets tested, and if the channel bottom breaks, the MA100 is the next level that has historically absorbed selling pressure on the daily chart. The $2,149–$2,180 zone is therefore the support cluster that the current move is approaching from above.
A daily close above the MA50 at $2,254, with RSI recovering above its signal line at 51.12, would confirm the channel bottom bounce has cleared its primary resistance and the path toward Ali Charts' $2,280 mid-range target is open.
A daily close below the MA100 at $2,149, breaching the channel bottom and then the daily MA100 support in sequence, would indicate the descending channel's lower boundary has failed and the next support reference requires identifying below the current structure.
#ETH

​The broader cryptocurrency market is experiencing a wave of renewed volatility, and Ethereum (ETH) is bearing the brunt of the selling pressure. After spending weeks tightly bound within a consolidating range, the second-largest cryptocurrency by market cap has finally broken to the downside, dipping below the crucial $2,200 psychological and technical support level.

​Why the $2,200 Mark Matters

​For the past month, the $2,220–$2,250 zone acted as a sturdy floor for buyers, absorbing selling pressure whenever ETH faced rejection near its $2,400 overhead resistance. However, a steady unwinding of long positions, negative technical indicators (including a fading Relative Strength Index and a bearish MACD crossover), and a recent surge in spot ETF outflows have weakened the bulls' defense.

​The breakdown below $2,200 marks a significant shift in short-term market structure, moving the conversation from a potential "imminent recovery" to a search for a new macro bottom.

​What Lies Ahead for ETH?

​Market analysts are now closely monitoring how Ethereum reacts to this breakdown. If the asset cannot quickly reclaim the $2,200 level as support, the technical doors swing open for further downside testing.

​The Downside Targets: Immediate dynamic support sits around the $2,150 mark (aligned with the 100-day moving average), followed by the vital $2,100 horizontal floor. A deeper slide could trigger major structural damage, pushing the token toward the $2,000 psychological baseline.

​The Silver Lining: On-chain analytics suggest that a portion of the recent selling has come from long-term holders securing profits rather than panic-selling retail investors. Additionally, fundamental updates on the horizon—like the highly anticipated Glamsterdam upgrade targeted for June, which aims to vastly improve Layer 1 transaction throughput—remain strong long-term catalysts that the market has yet to fully price in.

#ETH 3 minutes to clarify a trading truth:
Most people lose money because they're positioned like a 'gambler'.
I just calculate probabilities.

In 2014, I entered the market with 3000U.

During those years, people around me were getting liquidated, borrowing money to recover losses, and some even mortgaged their houses.
Meanwhile, my account's curve steadily went upward, with a maximum drawdown never exceeding 8%.
I don’t rely on insider info or K-line mysticism; I do one thing:
Treat the market like a slot machine and position myself as the house.

The core is just three points:

1. Lock in profits before discussing compound interest.
Any money that hasn’t hit my wallet isn’t profit.
Every time I place an order, I set both take profit and stop loss simultaneously.
When my account profit reaches 10% of the principal, I immediately withdraw 50% of the profit to a cold wallet,
and use the 'house money' to keep rolling.
If the market is trending, I eat compound interest;
if the market reverses, I only give back some profits, keeping my principal safe.

In 7 years, I've withdrawn profits over 40 times,

with a maximum withdrawal of 210,000 U in one week, even getting flagged by the exchange's risk control.

2. Dislocated positioning to earn money from liquidation points.

The market spends 80% of the time consolidating.
I look at three timeframes simultaneously:
Daily for direction, 4-hour for range, 15-minute for execution.
I split the same coin into two orders:

Order A goes with the trend, Order B goes against it.
Both orders have stop losses ≤ 1.5% of the principal,
with take profits at least 5 times the risk.
In a single-direction market, I profit from the trend;
in a consolidating market, while others get repeatedly stopped out, I harvest from both sides.

3. A stop loss isn’t failure; it’s a ticket.

Making money doesn’t rely on win rates but on positive expectation.
My win rate is only 38%,
but my risk-reward ratio has been over 4.5:1 in the long run.

Every 1 unit lost is a trial cost;
earning once covers multiple small losses.
When the market is right, let the profits run;
if not, exit immediately.
Catching two trends in a year can outperform most financial products.

Finally, three ironclad rules:

Split funds into 10 parts, with a maximum of 1 part per trade.
Never hold more than 3 positions at the same time.
If I lose 2 trades in a row, I immediately shut down and never open a 'revenge trade'.
For every doubling of the account, withdraw 20% to allocate to U.S. Treasuries or gold, staying secure even in a bear market.

Remember this: 
The market doesn’t fear your mistakes; it fears that you can’t get back up after a liquidation.

把市场当成赌博机，把自己放在庄家的位置

核心只有三点

一、先锁利润，再谈复利
没进自己钱包的钱，都不算赚。
每次下单，我同时挂好止盈和止损。
当账户盈利达到本金 10%，立刻提走 50% 利润 到冷钱包，
剩下的用“白来的钱”继续滚。
行情顺，就吃复利；
行情反转，最多回吐部分利润，本金始终安全。

7年里我提过40 多次盈利，

最多一周提走 21 万 U，甚至被交易所风控核查。

二、错位建仓，专赚爆仓点的钱

市场 80% 时间都在震荡。
我同时看三个周期：
日线定方向，4 小时找区间，15 分钟执行。
同一币种拆成两单：

A 单顺势突破，B 单逆向埋伏
两单止损都 ≤ 本金 1.5%，
止盈至少是风险的 5 倍。
行情单边我吃趋势，
行情震荡别人被反复扫损，我两头收割。

三、止损不是失败，是门票

赚钱靠的不是胜率，而是正期望。
我的胜率只有 38%，
但盈亏比长期在 4.5:1 以上。

每亏 1 块，是试错成本；
赚一次，覆盖多次小亏。
行情对了，让利润奔跑；
不对，立刻离场。
一年抓到两段趋势，就能跑赢绝大多数理财。

最后 3 条铁律

资金拆成 10 份，一单最多 1 份
同时持仓不超 3 份
连亏 2 单立刻关机，绝不开“复仇单”
账户每翻一倍，提走 20% 配置美债或黄金，熊市也安心。

记住一句话：
市场不怕你错，只怕你爆仓后再也站不起来

#ETH If it wasn't for that day I got liquidated,
maybe I would still be just an ordinary worker.

I knew my rule was:
'Risk no more than 2% per trade.'
But I told myself:
'The market is so smooth, this time it won't go wrong.'
So I started to go heavy, leverage up, and let profits ride.
At first, the market did indeed charge in my direction.
I even started fantasizing about doubling my account,
and I preemptively took a screenshot to post on social media.
Then the next second,
a breaking news hit, causing the market to reverse.
I didn't set my stop-loss properly, and the slippage was severe.

my account went from a 20% gain to zeroed out.
That night,
I sat alone in front of the computer for 3 hours without saying a word.
Not because of the loss.
But because for the first time I realized:
What I lost was not just capital.
But also my calm, confidence, and discipline.
Later, I finally understood—
I wasn't really learning to trade before.
I was just learning:
how to make money faster.
But real trading
is never about who has the better skills.
It's about who can control themselves.
After the liquidation, I began to force myself to change:
Write a plan before each trade;
Once the stop-loss is triggered, never hold on stubbornly;
Treat trading as a profession, not a gamble.
To be honest,
I'm still not some 'master.'
But at least, I've finally started to act like a real trader.
If you're currently losing, confused, or doubting life,
don't be afraid.
Many truly mature traders
awaken from a heart-wrenching liquidation.
Because the market's greatest teacher
has never been profit.
It's that zeroing out that keeps you up at night.

title: The Market Tests Conviction Before Rewarding It.
subTitle:
Many investors believe good decisions should produce immediate results. So when price moves slowly… or uncertainty increases… doubt begins to grow.
They start questioning: the strategy, the timing, and even themselves. But markets rarely reward conviction instantly. Before major moves, there is often: hesitation, volatility, and emotional pressure.
This is where many investors exit too early. Not because the idea was wrong but because the waiting became uncomfortable. Experienced investors understand: The market often tests conviction before rewarding it. Because if every opportunity felt easy, everyone would hold long enough to benefit from it.
🔑 Key Takeaway:  Patience is difficult because conviction is usually tested before results appear.
🧠 Practical Rule:  When doubt appears, ask yourself: “Has the thesis changed or has my emotional tolerance changed?” Those are not the same thing.
Systems over emotion. Conviction over noise.

#ETH  turning 1000U into 20000U wasn't just luck.
It was about getting wrecked by the market and finally learning to 'survive'.
Back in 2025 when I first entered forex, I was just like most traders:
Chasing after spikes and getting in at the top;
Always hoping for a big win, only to face liquidation time and again;
Holding onto losing positions instead of stopping out at 20%, and then getting wrecked;
Taking small profits but missing out on major trends.
At my worst, I was staring at the candlestick at 3 AM, watching my position get liquidated.
In that moment, I realized:
The market shows no mercy.
It only rewards those with discipline.
Eventually, I rolled that 1000U into 20000U by sticking to 5 ironclad rules.
First rule: 333 position sizing.
Never go all in.
With a 1000U bankroll, my first trade uses at most 330U.
If it dips, I've got bullets to average down; if it rises, I can keep riding the trend.
Second rule: 20% stop-loss rule.
Before entering a trade, think about how much you could lose, not how much you could gain.
A stop-loss isn't admitting defeat,
it's giving yourself another shot at recovery.
Third rule: double take-profit.
When you’ve doubled your profit, take it and don’t chase the last bit.
Real winners never dream of selling at the peak.
Fourth rule: withdraw profits.
Money earned that isn’t withdrawn is just numbers on a screen.
Fifth rule: low leverage, ride the trend.
In a bad market, losses are minimized; in a good market, go all in.
Many people enter the market, dreaming of instant riches.
But those who truly succeed study only one thing:
how to stay in the game longer.
Because as long as you're still at the table,
the next opportunity will surely come your way.
If you're currently facing losses, liquidation, or confusion,
remember this:
In crypto and forex, in the end,
it's not about the skills,
it's about discipline.

#ETH 从1000U做到20000U，我靠的不是运气。
而是被市场狠狠干过之后，终于学会了“活下来”。
2025年刚进外汇时，我和大多数人一样：
看到暴涨就追，结果买在山顶；
总想着一把翻身，结果一次次爆仓；
亏20%不舍得止损，最后直接腰斩；
赚一点就跑，却总错过大行情。
最惨的时候，凌晨3点盯着K线，看着仓位被强平。
那一刻我才明白：
市场不会同情任何人。
它只奖励有纪律的人。
后来，我靠5条铁律，硬生生把1000U滚到了20000U。
第一条：333建仓法。
永远别满仓。
1000U本金，首单最多只用330U。
跌了还有子弹补仓，涨了还能继续吃趋势。
第二条：20%止损铁律。
开单先想亏多少，而不是赚多少。
止损不是认输，
是给自己留下一次翻身机会。
第三条：翻倍止盈。
赚到翻倍就走，不吃最后一口。
真正赚钱的人，从不幻想卖在最高点。
第四条：盈利提现。
赚的钱，不提现永远只是数字。
第五条：低杠杆，顺趋势。
行情差少亏，行情好狠狠干。
很多人进市场，天天研究暴富。
但真正能走出来的人，研究的只有一件事：
怎么活得更久。
因为只要你还在牌桌上，
下一次机会，就一定轮得到你。
如果你现在也还在亏损、爆仓、迷茫，
记住一句话：
币圈和外汇，拼到最后，
拼的不是技术，
而是纪律。

This whale address is quite interesting.

In 2016, they bought 11,004 ETH at an average price of $3.45, ultimately making a profit of $30.38 million. Any normal person seeing this would likely think: Wow, the ancient whale is back.

But what’s really noteworthy isn’t that they bought 647 ETH this time, but that this address still holds $14.19 million USDC.

This shows that they’re not just "HODLing" or going all-in again. They’re simply taking a small portion of their cash after a year to buy a bit more ETH.

Retail traders often misunderstand smart money. When a whale buys a bit, retail sees it as a confirmation of a bull market; when a whale sells a bit, retail thinks it’s the end of the world; and when a whale holds cash, most retail traders don’t even notice.

The current picture is quite subtle: an address that once bought ETH at $3.45 is now only testing the waters with about $1.43 million. A bunch of traders who averaged $3,000 are already starting to write bull market declarations for them.

This reflects the high respect market participants have for smart money, while generally ignoring proper position management. To be honest, whether $ETH  gets a seat at the table in the next bull market is questionable, so don’t be blindly optimistic. Bottom fishing isn’t as good as picking $BTC #ETH .

content:
这个鲸鱼地址挺有意思。

2016 年用 3.45 美元均价买了 11004 枚 ETH，最后赚了 3038 万美元。正常人看到这里，第一反应肯定是：卧槽，远古巨鲸回来了。

但真正值得看的，不是他这次买了 647 枚 ETH，而是这个地址现在还有 1419 万 USDC。

这说明人家不是“信仰充值”，也不是“梭哈回归”。人家只是隔了一年，拿账户里一小部分现金，重新买一点 ETH。

散户最容易误会聪明钱。巨鲸买一点，散户理解成牛市确认；巨鲸卖一点，散户理解成世界末日；巨鲸留着现金，散户一般看不见。

现在的画面很微妙：一个曾经 3.45 美元买 ETH 的地址，只拿了约 143 万美元试仓。一群均价 3000 美元的人，已经开始替他写牛市宣言。

title: ألا يبدو الرسم البياني غريبًا قليلًا؟👀
subTitle:
في الوقت الذي أصبح فيه معظم السوق في حالة يأس تجاه ‏$ETH، بدأت الحركة تبدو أكثر إثارة للاهتمام بالنسبة لي.
نعم، مؤشر RSI يبدو ضعيفًا للغاية، وMACD ما زال سلبيًا، والسعر يتحرك أسفل المتوسطات المتحركة ‏MA20 وMA50… لكن الشيء اللافت هو أن الفوضى البيعية العنيفة التي ترافق عادةً الانهيارات الحقيقية ليست موجودة حتى الآن.
كنت أراقب تفاعل السعر مع منطقة فيبوناتشي لساعات اليوم. في لحظة معينة بدا الارتداد وكأنه مجرد سحب سيولة أو “Fake Bounce”، لكن رغم ذلك عاد المشترون للدفاع وبدأت الشموع تتعافى تدريجيًا. 🤔
بصراحة، زوج ‏ETH/BTC لا يزال ضعيفًا جدًا، وينزف ببطء يومًا بعد يوم. كما أن تدفقات ETF لا تساعد كثيرًا في تحسين المعنويات.
لكن المثير للاهتمام هو أن الإيثريوم، رغم كل السرد السلبي المحيط به، لم ينهار فعليًا حتى الآن.
وهذا يعطيني شعورًا يشبه المراحل التي سبقت انطلاقة 2024…
عندما كان الجميع يعلن أن ETH انتهى، وأن حلول ‏L2 ستسحب كل القيمة، وأن رواية الغاز ماتت… ثم فجأة انفجرت السوق بعنف وفاجأت الجميع. 🚀
لا أقول إن السيناريو سيتكرر بنفس الشكل… لكن أحيانًا الرسم البياني يهمس قبل أن تتغير نفسية الحشود.
📌 منطقة ‏$2,100 – $2,150 تبدو حاسمة جدًا حاليًا، لأنها المنطقة التي يواصل المشترون الدفاع عنها مرارًا. لكن المفارقة أن السوق يحب دائمًا تحويل “الدعم الواضح” إلى فخ نفسي للمتداولين.
أحيانًا لا ينهار السوق بالخوف…
بل يُرهق الناس بالملل ونفاد الصبر.
شيء آخر لفت انتباهي:
عندما يرتد ‏$BTC قليلًا، لا يتفاعل ‏ETH بقوة.
لكن عندما يتحرك الإيثريوم فعلًا، تكون الحركة غالبًا سريعة وعنيفة، وكأن الضغط يتراكم بصمت قبل الانفجار. 👀
ترقية ‏Pectra تبدو حتى الآن غير مُسعّرة بالكامل، كما أن تدفقات ‏RWA بدأت ترتفع تدريجيًا.
لكن الحقيقة أن السوق حاليًا لا يتحرك بالأساسيات فقط… بل يتمحور أكثر حول التموضع والسيولة.
بصراحة؟
أنا لست متفائلًا بالكامل… ولست هابطًا بالكامل أيضًا.
هذه المرحلة تبدو وكأنها اختبار حقيقي للصبر والانضباط.
الرسم البياني يتصرف وكأن شيئًا ما يُبنى تحت السطح… لكن السوق لم يستوعب ذلك بعد. 🤔🔥
